free_tier.stated: No free trial and no free tier: plans start at $20/month, charged when you subscribe. The first month is charged at signup and the plan renews monthly until cancelled. Sign-up alone, the docs and the dashboard need no card, but creating a sandbox answers 402 payment_method_required until one is added.
free_tier.notes: Each plan dollar comes back as machine time, so the $20 plan includes a month of machine time at the listed per-size rates; it does not roll over. A wallet with no plan can hold 10 GB of stopped-sandbox storage, but cannot start a sandbox.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the offer is a whole microVM with a disk ceiling per size, not an object store; no per-object cap is published
per_object_cap.notes: Disk is 12 GB on small, 50 GB on default, 125 GB on large and 251 GB on xlarge. SDK and MCP file reads are capped at 5 MiB and SDK downloads at 50 MiB, which are API call limits rather than a stored-object cap.

retention.stated: A stopped sandbox's disk, memory snapshot and automatic snapshots are kept at no charge for 14 days after it last stopped; named snapshots are kept until deleted. Storage counts toward the plan's included storage (50 GB on the $20 plan).
retention.notes: Going over the included storage does not delete anything unless auto-delete is turned on in Billing -> Storage. Running sandboxes do not count toward the storage allowance.

egress.terms: Bandwidth is not billed: the pricing FAQ answers 'Do you bill bandwidth?' with 'No.' Each sandbox has a public IPv6 address, an HTTPS URL for any port and outbound access to the internet; other sandboxes, private ranges and port 25 are blocked. There is no egress allowlist; the caller restricts outbound traffic inside the VM.

interface_detail: A REST API at https://sandboxer.com/api/v1 described by an OpenAPI spec at https://sandboxer.com/openapi.yaml, the sbx CLI, TypeScript and Python SDKs, a hosted MCP server at https://sandboxer.com/mcp, and a Daytona-compatible API at https://sandboxer.com/daytona/api. SSH and SCP reach each sandbox; any port can be published as a private-by-default HTTPS URL.
tooling: curl -fsSL https://sandboxer.com/install | sh installs the sbx CLI on macOS, Linux and Windows; npm i sandboxer-sdk and pip install sandboxer-sdk supply the SDKs; an MCP server, a Daytona-compatible API and SSH are also published. Erlang/Elixir and other language callers can use the REST API.
chaining: A hosted Ubuntu microVM per agent with Docker, systemd, nested KVM and preinstalled coding agents, billed per second and free while stopped, so parallel agent fleets and snapshot-based forks share one API without provisioning hardware.

limits.value: $20/month plan includes one month of machine time at the listed rates: $0.018/h small, $0.036/h default, $0.072/h large, $0.20/h xlarge; time does not roll over
starts limited per rolling minute, hour and day on the $20 plan at 12 / 60 / 200; API calls limited to 600 a minute per key
stopped sandboxes and automatic snapshots are kept 14 days after last stop; included storage 50 GB on the $20 plan

limits_note: The $20 plan allows 100 sandboxes active at once; xlarge needs the $100 plan or higher. Above a start limit, up to 3x the limit, a paid start costs $0.03, $0.05 or $0.07 by bracket from prepaid credit; a start past 3x is refused with 429.
binding_note: There is no free allowance at all, so the $20 monthly charge is the first gate; for that plan the included machine time and the 100-active-sandbox concurrency cap are what run out first under load. A default sandbox at $0.036 an hour would cost $26.28 if left on for 730 hours, more than the plan's $20 of included time.

identity_cost.detail: Signing up needs no card: 'Why do you need a card? Every sandbox is a real machine with a public address, so a card keeps abuse down. You can sign up, read the docs and look around the dashboard without one.' Choosing a plan adds a card and charges the first month immediately, and creating a sandbox without a card answers 402 payment_method_required. No phone number, ID document or institution is named on the pages read.

reliability_note: No SLA during early access. A wallet at zero keeps running sandboxes for a 24-hour grace period, then stops them with memory and disk kept; out-of-hours the API returns 402 billing_required. Starts are refused at 3x the per-window limit with 429, and capacity can return 503 no_ready_machine or capacity_exceeded.
confidence_note: The vendor's own pricing page, pricing.md, llms.txt, FAQ, limits, billing and signup pages were read on 2026-11-24; the rate table and free-tier answer are from those pages. The live identity gate beyond the published signup text is unverified.
